title: Kurdish Peace Process Moves to Implementation as Oversight Board Meets; CBRT Resumes One-Week Repo Auctions, Banks Rally
subhead: Ankara's landmark PKK reintegration law enters its operational phase with the oversight board convening and Öcalan set to join a disarmament subcommittee, while the central bank restores its main funding channel after a six-month Iran-war suspension and Goldman raises lira forecasts.

sections.heading: Kurdish Peace Process Enters Implementation Phase
sections.body: The Turkish parliament's landmark PKK reintegration law moved from statute to operation this week. According to Turkish Minute, pro-Kurdish DEM Party lawmaker Pervin Buldan said the main oversight board would meet on August 24 and then begin setting up subcommittees, with jailed PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan expected to join a subcommittee overseeing the group's laying down of arms and helping arrange the return of fighters who disarm. The law, approved by President Erdoğan and published in the Official Gazette on August 18, creates an oversight board led by the vice president and composed of key ministers and security chiefs; it can defer probes, trials and prison terms for five or ten years once the National Security Council confirms the PKK has disarmed and dissolved. Öcalan himself is excluded from relief because the law bars amnesty for life-term prisoners convicted of crimes before June 1, 2005.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the first concrete institutional step toward ending a conflict that has killed more than 40,000 people since 1984. The board's composition and the subcommittee structure will determine whether disarmament is verifiable enough to trigger the MGK's confirmation — the real test of whether the process survives contact with implementation.

sections.heading: CBRT Resumes One-Week Repo Auctions, Banks Rally
sections.body: The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) resumed one-week repo auctions on Monday after suspending them on March 1 as part of its response to the Iran-war shock. According to Türkiye Today, the bank conducted a ₺1 billion ($20.8 million) auction at a 37% simple rate (44.6% compound), shifting funding back toward its policy rate after banks had been forced onto more expensive 40% overnight funding. Banking shares on Borsa Istanbul jumped over 4%, and the BIST 100 opened 0.9% higher at 14,637. ING called the move a positive signal, noting the March suspension had effectively amounted to a 300-basis-point rate increase. The 2-year benchmark Treasury yield fell to 40.2%.
sections.whyItMatters: Restoring the repo channel signals growing official confidence in financial stability after six months of war-driven tightening. It also eases funding costs for banks and supports carry-trade positions, but it comes as the lira keeps sliding — a tension the central bank will have to manage carefully.

sections.heading: Goldman Raises Lira Forecasts as Depreciation Pressure Mounts
sections.body: Goldman Sachs raised its USD/TRY forecasts on Monday, citing the lira's pace of monthly depreciation. According to Türkiye Today, the dollar hovered near 48.1 on August 24, up 1.8% for the month and nearly matching the expected ~2% August inflation rate. Goldman lifted its three-month forecast to 51 from 48, six-month to 53 from 50, and 12-month to 59 from 54, warning that risks tilt toward faster depreciation unless energy prices fall significantly, gold rises sharply, or the dollar weakens broadly. The bank also flagged mounting pressure on the external balance and rising election-related volatility, while maintaining its view that the current exchange-rate regime remains in place.
sections.whyItMatters: The lira is depreciating at roughly the pace of inflation, which keeps real appreciation elusive and complicates the disinflation story. Goldman's forecast path implies continued managed depreciation rather than a step-change, but the election-cycle volatility it cites is a growing wildcard.

sections.heading: Israel-Turkey Rivalry Over Syria's Airspace Persists
sections.body: The standoff over Syria's skies continues to simmer. The New Arab reports that Israeli jets struck Syria's Abu al-Duhur Air Base eight times on August 18, with Tel Aviv claiming it pre-empted a Turkish military deployment there; Ankara denied any delegation was at the base before or during the attack. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani rejected claims Turkey planned to establish a base at Abu al-Duhur, saying the site was being restored for the Syrian Air Force. ACLED's Muaz Al Abdullah told The New Arab that pressure on Israel's freedom of action in Syria appears to be increasing, with a notable decline in Israeli airstrikes since August 2025 even as ground incursions continue — suggesting Israel is reserving air power for moments when other measures prove insufficient.
sections.whyItMatters: Syria's airspace remains contested between two US-equipped neighbors rather than controlled by Damascus. The pattern — fewer Israeli airstrikes but persistent ground operations — suggests Israel is adapting its posture as Turkey incrementally tests its aerial dominance, keeping the risk of a direct clash alive.

sections.heading: Ankara Widens Crackdown on Anti-Erdoğan Islamist Groups
sections.body: Turkish authorities detained 32 members of the Furkan Foundation, an Adana-based Islamist group known for staunch opposition to President Erdoğan, in an operation last week, according to Medyascope. The arrests included founder and leader Alparslan Kuytul and his wife Semra; authorities also blocked access to 349 associated social media accounts and appointed trustees to five companies. The Justice Ministry cited charges of founding and running a criminal organization, money laundering, document falsification and aggravated fraud. The operation follows a mid-August crackdown on the Süleymancı cemaat, another anti-Erdoğan Islamist group, and came after an Erdoğan adviser publicly warned Kuytul, 'You will be next.'
sections.whyItMatters: The back-to-back operations against two independent Islamist networks — groups outside the state-aligned religious establishment — signal a deliberate effort to consolidate control over the religious field ahead of the election cycle, using financial and criminal charges rather than political ones.

bottomLine: Turkey's most consequential development today is the Kurdish peace process crossing from legislation into implementation: the oversight board has convened and Öcalan is set to join the disarmament subcommittee, the first real test of whether the 40,000-death conflict can be wound down. On the economic front, the CBRT's resumption of one-week repo auctions after a six-month suspension is a clear confidence signal that lifted bank stocks, even as Goldman's higher lira forecasts underscore that depreciation pressure has not gone away. The Israel-Turkey rivalry over Syria's airspace and Ankara's widening crackdown on independent Islamist groups round out a day of incremental but meaningful movement across politics, economy and regional security.
sources: Turkish Minute, Türkiye Today, The New Arab, Medyascope, The World (PRX/DW), Daily Sabah, Bloomberg
